pp:ce:2014:q29-s2.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 2 | Question: 29
pp:ce:2014:q29-s2.question: Water is flowing at a steady rate through a homogeneous and saturated horizontal soil strip of 10 m length. The strip is being subjected to a constant water head(H) of 5 m at the beginning and 1 m at the end. If the governing equation of flow in the soil strip is $\frac{d^{2}H}{dx^2}=0$ (where x is the distance along the soil strip), the value of H (in m) at the middle of the strip is ________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Given, equation of the flow of soil strip is

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{d^{2} H}{d x^{2}}&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{H}}{\mathrm{d} x}&=\mathrm{C}_{1} \\ \Rightarrow \quad H&=C_{1} x+C_{2} \\ \text{at }x=0, H=&5 \mathrm{m} \\ \Rightarrow \quad C_{2}&=5 \\ \Rightarrow \quad H&=C_{1} x+5 \\ \text{at }x&=10, H=1 \mathrm{m} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 1&=C_{1} \times 10+5 \\ \Rightarrow \quad 10 C_{1}&=-4 \\ \Rightarrow \quad C_{1}&=-\frac{2}{5} \\ \Rightarrow \quad H&=-\frac{2}{5} x+5 \\ \text{at }x&=5 \mathrm{m} \\ H&=-\frac{2}{5} \times 5+5 \\ H&=3 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2014:q39-s2.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 2 | Question: 39
pp:ce:2014:q39-s2.question: A single vertical friction pile of diameter 500 mm and length 20 m is subjected to a vertical compressive load. The pile is embedded in a homogeneous sandy stratum where: angle of internal friction is $\phi=30^{\circ}$, dry unit weight $(\gamma _{d})=20 kN/m^{3}$ and angle of wall friction is $\delta =2\varphi /3$. Considering the coefficient of lateral earth pressure (K)=2.7 and the bearing capacity factor ($N_q$)=25, the ultimate bearing capacity of the pile (in kN) is________

detailed_solution.markdown: Homogeneous sandy stratum $$\begin{aligned} \phi &=30^{\circ} \\ \gamma_{d} &=20 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned}$$ Wall friction angle. $\delta=\frac{2}{3} \phi=\frac{2}{3} \times 30=20^{\circ}$ Lateral earth pressure coefficient, $K=2.7$ Bearing capacity factor, $N_{q}=25$ Ultimate load capacity, $Q_{u}=?$ Vertical effective stress at 20m. $\overline{\sigma_{v}}=20 \times 20=400 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$ From 0 to 20m, unit point bearing resistance and skin friction resistance remain constant at $\overline{\sigma_{\mathrm{v}}}=400 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$ The ultimate load capacity is given by $$\begin{aligned} Q_{u}&=q_{\mathrm{up}} \cdot A_{p}+q_{\mathrm{s}} \cdot A_{s}\\ &=f_{s}\left(Q_{u p}=0\right. for friction pile) \\ \text{where}\quad q_{s}&=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \overline{\sigma_{v}} \cdot K \cdot \tan \delta\\ &=\frac{1}{2} \times 400 \times 2.7 \tan 20^{\circ} \\ &=196.54 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$$ Skin friction resistance, $$\begin{aligned} Q_{u}=f_{s} &=196.54 \times \pi \times 0.5 \times 20 \\ &=6174.49 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}$$

detailed_solution.markdown: Diameter of throat, $d=0.1 \mathrm{m}$ Diameter of pipe, $D=0.2 \mathrm{m}$ Pressure difference, $\frac{P_{1}-P_{2}}{w}=2 m=h$ Coefficient of discharge $C_{D}=1$ Discharge, $$\begin{aligned} Q&=\frac{C_{D} A_{1} A_{2} \sqrt{2 g h}}{\sqrt{A_{1}^{2}-A_{2}^{2}}}\\ A_{1} &=\frac{\pi}{4}(0.2)^{2} \\ \text { and } A_{2} &=\frac{\pi}{4}(0.1)^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad Q &=\frac{1 \times\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)^{2} \times(0.2)^{2}(0.1)^{2} \sqrt{2 \times 9.81 \times 2}}{\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \sqrt{(0.2)^{4}-(0.1)^{4}}} \\ &=0.0508=0.050 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{sec} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2014:q43-s2.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 2 | Question: 43
pp:ce:2014:q43-s2.question: A rectangular channel of 2.5 m width is carrying a discharge of 4 $m^3$/s. Considering that acceleration due to gravity as 9.81 m/$s^2$, the velocity of flow (in m/s) corresponding to the critical depth (at which the specific energy is minimum) is _______

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Open Channel Flow
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} Q &=4 m^{3} / s, B=2.5 m \\ \Rightarrow \quad q &=\frac{4}{2.5} m^{3} / s / m \\ &=1.6 m^{3} / s / m \\ y_{c}^{3} &=\frac{q^{2}}{g} \Rightarrow y_{c}=0.639 m \end{aligned}$$

At critical depth velocity head $=\frac{y_{c}}{2}$

$$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad \frac{V^{2}}{2 g}&=\frac{0.639}{2}\\ \Rightarrow V&=\sqrt{0.639 \times 9} \\ &=2.504 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2014:q44-s2.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 2 | Question: 44
pp:ce:2014:q44-s2.question: Irrigation water is to be provided to a crop in a field to bring the moisture content of the soil from the existing 18% to the field capacity of the soil at 28%. The effective root zone of the crop is 70 cm. If the densities of the soil and water are 1.3 g/$cm^2$ and 1.0 g/$cm^3$respectively, the depth of irrigation water (in mm) required for irrigating the crop is ________

detailed_solution.markdown:
Given,

Root zone depth,

$d=70 \mathrm{cm}$

Field capacity,

$F_{C}=28 \%$

Existing moisture content,

$w=18 \%$

Density of soil,

$\gamma=1.3 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$

Density of water,

$\gamma_{w}=1.0 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$

Depth of irrigation water required,

$$\begin{aligned} d_{w} &=\frac{\gamma}{\gamma_{w}} d\left(F_{c}-w\right) \\ &=\frac{1.3}{1.0} \times(70 \times 10)(28 \%-18 \%) \\ &=1.3 \times(70 \times 10) \times \frac{10}{100} \\ &=91 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2014:q45-s2.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 2 | Question: 45
pp:ce:2014:q45-s2.question:
With reference to a standard Cartesian (x,y) plane, the parabolic velocity distribution profile of fully developed laminar flow in x-direction between two parallel, stationary and identical plates that are separated by distance, h, is given by the expression
$u=-\frac{h^{2}}{8\mu }\frac{\mathrm{d} p}{\mathrm{d} x}\left [ 1-4(\frac{y}{h})^{2} \right ]$
In this equation, the y=0 axis lies equidistant between the plates at a distance h/2 from the two plates, p is the pressure variable and $\mu$ is the dynamic viscosity term. The maximum and average velocities are, respectively

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Viscous Flow of Incompressible Fluid
detailed_solution.markdown: Velocily expression for a laminar flow between two parallel plates is $U=-\frac{n^{2}}{8 u}\left(\frac{d p}{d x}\right)\left[1-4\left(\frac{y}{n}\right)^{2}\right]$ End condition $U=U_{max}\text{ at }y=0$ $\Rightarrow U_{max} = -\frac{h^{2}}{8\mu}\left(\frac{dp}{dx} \right )$ Discharges dQ = Area x Velocily $\Rightarrow \Delta 0=\left[-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{8 \mu}\left(\frac{d \rho}{d x}\right)\left(1-4\left(\frac{y}{n}\right)^{2}\right)\right](d y \times 1)$ $$\begin{aligned} &\Rightarrow Q=-\frac{h^{2}}{8 \mu}\left(\frac{d p}{d x}\right) \int_{-h / 2}^{h / 2}\left(1-\frac{4 y^{2}}{h^{2}}\right) d y\\ &=-\frac{h^{2}}{8 \mu}\left(\frac{d p}{d x}\right)\left[y-\frac{4 y^{3}}{3 h^{2}}\right]_{-n / 2}^{h / 2}\\ &=-\frac{h^{2}}{8 \mu}\left(\frac{d p}{d x}\right)\left[\left\{\frac{h}{2}-\left(-\frac{h}{2}\right)\right\}-\left\{\frac{4}{3 h^{2}}\left(\frac{h^{3}}{8}-\left(-\frac{h^{3}}{8}\right)\right)\right\}\right]\\ &=-\frac{h^{3}}{12 \mu}\left(\frac{d p}{d x}\right)\\ &Q=A V\\ &-\frac{h^{3}}{12 \mu}\left(\frac{d p}{d x}\right)=(h \times 1) \times U_{a v g}\\ &\Rightarrow \quad U_{a v g}=-\frac{h^{2}}{12 \mu}\left(\frac{d p}{d x}\right) \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2014:q46-s2.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 2 | Question: 46
pp:ce:2014:q46-s2.question: A suspension of sand like particles in water with particles of diameter 0.10 mm and below is flowing into a settling tank at 0.10 $m^3$/s. Assume g=9.81 m/$s^{2}$, specific gravity of particles=2.65, and kinematic vescosity of water=$1.0105 \times 10^{-2} cm^{2}$/s. The minimum surface area (in $m^{2}$) required for this settling tank to remove particles of size 0.06 mm and above with 100% efficiency is_________

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} V_{s} &=\frac{\left(G_{s}-1\right) g d^{2}}{18 v} \\ &=\frac{(2.65-1) \times 9.81 \times\left(6 \times 10^{-2}\right)^{2}}{18 \times 1.0105 \times 10^{-2}} \\ &=\frac{1.65 \times 9.81 \times 36 \times 10^{-4}}{18 \times 1.0105 \times 10^{-2} \times 10^{2}} \\ &=3.204 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ V_{s} &=\frac{Q}{B L} \\ \Rightarrow\quad B L &=\frac{0.1}{3.204 \times 10^{-3}}=31.214 \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2014:q47-s2.question: A surface water treatment plant operates round the clock with a flow rate of 35 $m^{3}$/min. detailed_solution.markdown:

$$\begin{aligned} \text { Flow rate, } & Q=35 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{min} \\ & G t=4 \times 10^{4} \\ \text { Alum dosage } &=25 \mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{lit} . \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2014:q48-s2.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 2 | Question: 48
pp:ce:2014:q48-s2.question: An effluent at a flow rate of 2670 $m^{3}$/d from a sewage treatment plant is to be disinfected. The laboratory data of disinfection studies with a chlorine dosage of 15 mg/l yield the model $N_{t}=N_{o}e^{-0.145t}$  where $N_t$= number of micro-organisms surviving at time t (in min.) and $N_o$= number of micro-organism present initially (at t=0). The volume of disinfection unit (in $m^{3}$) required to achieve a 98% kill of micro-organisms is______

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} Q&=2670 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{d} \\ N_{t}&=\mathrm{No} . \mathrm{e}^{-0.145 \mathrm{t}} \end{aligned}$$

Let x be the no. of microorganisms (M.O.) present initially.

98% kill of M.O. imlies that at time 't' 2% of M.O. are still surviving

$\therefore$ M.O. surviving at time 't' $=\frac{2}{100} x$

$$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \frac{2}{100} x &=x \cdot \mathrm{e}^{-0.145 \mathrm{t}} \\ \therefore \qquad t &=26.979 \mathrm{min} \\ t &=0.018736 \text { days } \\ \therefore \qquad \text { Volume } &=Q . t \\ &=2670 \times 0.018736 \\ &=50.0244 \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2014:q49-s2.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 2 | Question: 49
pp:ce:2014:q49-s2.question: A waste water stream (flow=2 $m^{3}$/s, ultimate BOD=90 mg/l) is joining a small river (flow=12 $m^{3}$/s, ultimate BOD=5 mg/l). Both water streams get mixed up instantaneously. Cross sectional area of the river is 50 $m^{2}$. Assuming the de-oxygenation rate constant, k'=0.25/day the BOD (in mg/l) of the river water, 10 km downstream of the mixing point is

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Treatment of Waste Water
detailed_solution.markdown:
Flow of waste water stream,

$Q_{w}=2 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{sec}$

Ultimate BOD,

$Y_{w}=90 \mathrm{mg} / l=90 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$

Flow of river,

$Q_{R}=12 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{sec}$

Ultimate BOD of river,

$Y_{R}=0.5 \mathrm{mg} / l=5 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$

BOD of mixture,

$$\begin{aligned} Y_{0} &=\frac{(2 \times 90)+(12 \times 5)}{2+12} \\ &=\frac{180+60}{14}=\frac{240}{14} \\ &=17.143 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ k_{D} &=0.434 \mathrm{K} \\ &=0.434 \times 0.25=0.1085 \\ Y_{t} &=Y_{0}\left[1-(10)^{-k_{0} t}\right] &\ldots(i)\\ \text { Area of river } &=50 \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \text { Flow of river } &=12 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{sec} \\ \text { Stream velocity } &=\frac{14}{50}=0.28 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{sec} \\ \text { Time taken, } & t=\frac{10 \mathrm{km}}{0.28 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}}=0.4133 \text { days } \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ From eq. (i),

$$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{BOD}_{\text {left }} &=Y_{0}-Y_{t} \\ &=Y_{0} \times 10^{-k t} \\ &=17.143 \times 10^{-0.1085 \times 0.4133} \\ &=15.46 \mathrm{mg} / l \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2014:q50-s2.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 2 | Question: 50
pp:ce:2014:q50-s2.question: In a Marshall sample, the bulk specific gravity of mix and aggregates are 2.324 and 2.546 respectively. The sample includes 5% of bitumen (by total weight of mix) of specific gravity 1.10. The theoretical maximum specific gravity of mix is 2.441. The void filled with bitumen (VFB) in the Marshall sample (in %) is _______

detailed_solution.markdown:
$V_{v}=\frac{G_{t}-G_{m}}{G_{t}} \times 100=\frac{2.441-2.324}{2.441} \times 100$

$=4.79 \%$

Void filled with bitumen,

$$\begin{array}{l} V_{b}=G_{m} \times \frac{W_{b}(\%)}{G_{b}}=2.324 \times \frac{5}{1.1}=10.56 \%\\ \mathrm{VMA}=V_{v}+V_{b}=4.79+10.56=15.35 \% \\ \therefore \mathrm{VFB}=\frac{V_{b}(\%)}{\mathrm{VMA}} \times 100=\frac{10.56}{15.35} \times 100=68.79 \% \end{array}$$

pp:ce:2014:q51-s2.question: A student riding a bicycle on a 5 km one-way street takes 40 minutes to reach home. The speed of vehicle stream on that road (in km/hr) is

Velocity of student $=\frac{5 k m}{(40-15) \min }$

$=12\mathrm{km} / \mathrm{hr}$

$\left(\frac{\text { Vehicle/min }}{\text { Relative speed of vehicle w.r.t. student }}\right)_{\text {moving}}$

$=\left(\frac{\text { Vehicle/min }}{\text { Relative speed of vehicle w.r.t. student }}\right)_{\text {standing }}$

$$\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad \frac{60 / 25}{x-12} &=\frac{45 / 15}{x-0} \\ \Rightarrow \quad x &=60 \mathrm{km} / \mathrm{hr} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2014:q52-s2.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 2 | Question: 52
pp:ce:2014:q52-s2.question: On a section of a highway the speed-density relationship is linear and is given by $v=[80-\frac{2}{3}k]$; where v is in km/h and k is in veh/km. The capacity (in veh/h) of this section of the highway would be

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} v&=80-\frac{2 k}{3} \\ \text{Capacity,}\quad &=v \times k \\ &=80 k-\frac{2 k^{2}}{3} \end{aligned}$$

For q to be maximum

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{d q}{d k}&=0\\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d q}{d k} &=80-\frac{4 k}{3}=0 \\ \Rightarrow k&=60 \end{aligned}$$

Maximum capacity,

$$\begin{aligned} q&=80 \times 60-\frac{2}{3}(60)^{2} \\ &=4800-\frac{2}{3} \times 3600 \\ &=2400 \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2014:q53-s2.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 2 | Question: 53
pp:ce:2014:q53-s2.question: A pre-timed four phase signal has critical lane flow rate for the first three phases as 200, 187 and 210 veh/hr with saturation flow rate of 1800 veh/hr/lane for all phases. The lost time is given as 4 seconds for each phase. If the cycle length is 60 seconds, the effective green time (in seconds) of the fourth phase is _________

detailed_solution.markdown:
Flow rates for the first three phase are given as

$$\begin{aligned} q_{1}&=200 \mathrm{veh} / \mathrm{hr} \\ q_{2}&=187 \mathrm{veh} / \mathrm{hr}\\ \text{and}\quad q_{3}&=210 \text { veh/hr } \end{aligned}$$

Saturation flow rate is 1800 veh/hr/lane

Lost time,

$L=4 \times 4=16 \mathrm{sec}$

Length of the cycle,

$C_{0}=60 \mathrm{sec}$

$$\begin{aligned} \text { Now, } \quad y_{1} &=\frac{q_{1}}{s_{1}}=\frac{200}{1800} \\ y_{2} &=\frac{q_{2}}{s_{2}}=\frac{187}{1800} \\ y_{3} &=\frac{q_{3}}{s_{3}}=\frac{210}{1800} \\ C_{0} &=\frac{1.5 L+5}{1-y} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 60 &=\frac{1.5 \times 16+5}{1-y}\\ \Rightarrow 60 &=\frac{24+5}{1-y} \\ \Rightarrow 1-y &=\frac{29}{60} \\ \Rightarrow \quad y&=\frac{1-29}{60}=\frac{60-29}{60} \\ &=0.517\\ \text{And}\quad y&=y_{1}+y_{2}+y_{3}+y_{4}\\ \Rightarrow \quad 0.517 &=\frac{597}{1800}+y_{4} \\ \Rightarrow \quad y_{4}&=0.185 \\ G &=\frac{y_{4}}{y}\left(C_{0}-L\right)\\ &=\frac{0.185}{0.517}(60-16) \\ &=15.745 \mathrm{sec} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2014:q54-s2.title: GATE CE 2014 | Set 2 | Question: 54
pp:ce:2014:q54-s2.question: A tachometer was placed at point P to estimate the horizontal distances PQ and PR. The corresponding stadia intercepts with the telescope kept horizontal, are 0.320 m and 0.210 m, respectively. The $\angle QPR$ is measured to be $61^{\circ}{30}'{30}''$. If the stadia multiplication constant=100 and stadia addition constant=0.10 m, the horizontal distance (in m) between the points Q and R is ________

detailed_solution.markdown:

Applying the cosine rule

$$\begin{array}{l} Q R=\sqrt{P Q^{2}+P R^{2}-2(P Q)(P R) \cos \theta} \\ \text { Where, } \theta=61^{\circ} 30^{\prime} 30^{\prime \prime}=61.508^{\circ} \\ =\sqrt{1030,41+445.21-2(32,1)(21,1) \cos 61.508^{\circ}} \\ =\sqrt{1030.41+445.21-646.2}=28.8 \mathrm{m} \end{array}$$

pp:ce:2014:q55-s2.question: The chainage of the intersection point of two straights is 1585.60 m and the angle of intersection is $140^{\circ}$. If the radius of a circular curve is 600.00 m, the tangent distance (in m) and length of the curve (in m), respectively are
